findings.explanation: The flagged sink at app/routes/orders.py:66 executes `session.execute(text("INSERT INTO orders (user_id, status, total) VALUES (:user_id, :status, :total)"), [...])`. The SQL string is a static literal with no interpolation, f-string, .format(), or concatenation of request-derived values. All dynamic values (user_id, status, total) are passed as a separate list of dicts bound to the `:name` placeholders, which is exactly the parameterized pattern mandated by security-policy.md §5. The values are also coerced to int/str/float before binding. No user-controlled input reaches the query text itself, so there is no SQL injection vector. This is a false positive of the heuristic rule.

evidence.content: All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters (SQLAlchemy `text()` with `:name` parameters, or DB-API placeholders with a separate params argument). String interpolation, f-strings, `%` formatting, `.format()`, or string concatenation of request-derived values into SQL is forbidden (CWE-89).

findings.explanation: The new POST /bulk endpoint accepts a JSON array of orders and inserts each row with a user-supplied `user_id` (int(item.get('user_id', 0))). It is gated only by @require_role('manager'), which permits any manager or admin to create orders attributed to ANY user_id — including arbitrary users. The policy (security-policy.md §3) states 'A user may view ONLY their own orders' and 'Listing another user's orders is restricted to that user themselves and administrators', and the api-spec.md orders table lists only `/orders` POST as 'any authenticated user (creates own order)' — there is no documented endpoint that allows creating orders on behalf of other users. The existing create_order() endpoint (app/routes/orders.py:19-33) correctly scopes to g.current_user.id. The new endpoint's manager-level role check is insufficient: it grants managers (not just admins) the ability to fabricate orders for arbitrary users, which is inconsistent with the policy's strict ownership model. The policy does not explicitly forbid a manager-level bulk import, so this is 'possible' rather than 'vulnerable', but the lack of an is_owner_or_admin check and the manager (not admin) role requirement make this a likely authorization flaw.

evidence.content: A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data. Listing another user's orders is restricted to that user themselves and administrators.
| `/orders` | POST | any authenticated user (creates own order) |

findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) restrict the endpoint to @require_role('admin') and validate that each item's user_id corresponds to a real user, or (b) remove the user-supplied user_id and force user_id=g.current_user.id for every row (matching the existing create_order pattern), or (c) add an is_owner_or_admin check per row so managers can only create orders for themselves and admins can create for any user. The current manager-level role with arbitrary user_id is inconsistent with the policy's ownership model.
